1.why: Body text uses a clean sans-serif with comfortable line height and monospaced codes, though letter spacing is standard rather than notably generous.

2.why: All instructions appear in sentence case with no italics and no dense paragraphs on any screen.

3.why: The narrow single-column card with large controls should read well on a phone, although only desktop-width screenshots were provided.

4.why: Prompts such as 'Enter the six-digit code sent to your phone' are brief and written in plain language.

5.why: The recovery-code field shows a format placeholder (ABCD-EFGH-IJKL-MNPQ), but the verification and authenticator code fields display no example of expected input.

6.why: The longest passage on any screen is two sentences, so the user never has to read a long block of text to proceed.

7.why: The setup secret and recovery codes are rendered as plain selectable text rather than images so they can be copied, but no dedicated copy button is provided.

8.why: No QR code or scanning equivalent is offered anywhere; step 4 requires manual entry of the secret and step 3 explicitly states a QR code is 'not required'.

9.why: The screenshots show plain input fields with no autocomplete suggestions, one-time-code prompt, or any other visible evidence of autofill or password-manager support.

10.why: Each screen has a bold heading naming the current step and a single prominent blue primary button.

11.why: Every step highlights one primary blue action with secondary options de-emphasised, though the red 'Log out' button on the MFA-active screen is fairly prominent.

12.why: Confirmations such as 'Recovery code accepted. It cannot be used again.' plainly state what happened, though the generic error message is less clear about the cause.

13.why: 'Start again' and retry-after-error are available without stated penalty and codes are shown unmasked, but there are no reveal/hide toggles or resend-code buttons.

14.why: The error 'We could not complete that request. Please try again.' is non-blaming but does not state the actual problem, namely that the entered code was incorrect.

15.why: Reading is untimed, but the SMS code 'expires in five minutes' and the authenticator code rotates every 30 seconds, so code entry is time-constrained rather than generous.
